This method is used for group-management checks without a specific group, for example GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup(). As a result, a permission granting only 'view' on the Groups resource type can authorize creation or top-level movement of groups. The check should require only MANAGE."

      "title": "getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs",
      "body": "In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the code calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and adds groupResource.getId() to the returned set. hasPermission expects a realm group ID because it looks up the authorization resource by name, and callers such as UsersResource put the returned set into UserModel.GROUPS to filter user searches by group membership. Authorization resource IDs are not realm group IDs, so the returned set is wrong. This breaks user search/count filtering based on group view-members permissions and can cause empty or inconsistent results."

      "title": "Per-instance authorization resources are created without a resource type",
      "body": "AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() creates authorization resources for individual clients, groups, and users but never calls resource.setType(resourceType). Only the type-level resources created during init() have a type. Consequently type-based lookups such as resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) in GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission cannot find instance resources, breaking enumeration of groups with permissions."

      "body": "AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns immediately if realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already present. Existing realms that initialized V2 before this change will not receive the new Groups scopes or the Groups type resource. Subsequent use of group permissions can fail with missing scopes or null type resources. Initialization should idempotently add missing scopes/resources to existing admin-permissions clients."
    },

When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 and groups() returns GroupPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException. This can cause group deletion failures or swallowed errors. If the V1 feature is disabled, the listener is not registered at all and V2 authorization resources may be orphaned. A V2-aware cleanup path is needed."

findings.title: canManage() treats VIEW permission on all groups as MANAGE
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() calls hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE). This method is used for group-management checks without a specific group, for example GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup(). As a result, a permission granting only 'view' on the Groups resource type can authorize creation or top-level movement of groups. The check should require only MANAGE.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the code calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and adds groupResource.getId() to the returned set. hasPermission expects a realm group ID because it looks up the authorization resource by name, and callers such as UsersResource put the returned set into UserModel.GROUPS to filter user searches by group membership. Authorization resource IDs are not realm group IDs, so the returned set is wrong. This breaks user search/count filtering based on group view-members permissions and can cause empty or inconsistent results.

findings.title: Per-instance authorization resources are created without a resource type
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() creates authorization resources for individual clients, groups, and users but never calls resource.setType(resourceType). Only the type-level resources created during init() have a type. Consequently type-based lookups such as resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) in GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission cannot find instance resources, breaking enumeration of groups with permissions.

findings.title: No migration of scopes/resources for existing admin-permissions clients
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns immediately if realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already present. Existing realms that initialized V2 before this change will not receive the new Groups scopes or the Groups type resource. Subsequent use of group permissions can fail with missing scopes or null type resources. Initialization should idempotently add missing scopes/resources to existing admin-permissions clients.

findings.title: Provider event cleanup is incompatible with V2 group permissions
findings.body: On GroupRemovedEvent the listener calls management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false). When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 and groups() returns GroupPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException. This can cause group deletion failures or swallowed errors. If the V1 feature is disabled, the listener is not registered at all and V2 authorization resources may be orphaned. A V2-aware cleanup path is needed.

findings.title: getScope can throw NullPointerException for unknown or missing resource type
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getScope() validates schema scopes with SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes() without checking whether resourceType is null or whether the map lookup returns null. Invalid or missing resource types will cause a NullPointerException instead of a ModelValidationException.

findings.title: Fallback to all-groups resource can NPE if the type resource is missing
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission() falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) and then calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource). getResourceTypeResource can return null if the Groups type resource was not initialized, leading to a NullPointerException. The same pattern exists in UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission. The code should handle a missing type resource gracefully.

findings.title: getResourceName does not handle the new Groups resource type
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName() only special-cases Users resources. For Groups resources it falls back to resource.getDisplayName(), but group instance resources are created with the group ID as the name and no display name. Administrative UI or policy representations may therefore show blank names for group resources.

findings.title: Javadoc for requireManageMembers is incorrect
findings.body: The Javadoc for requireManageMembers says it throws ForbiddenException if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false, but implementations check canManageMembers(GroupModel). The same interface also documents getGroupIdsWithViewPermission as returning a Stream while the method returns a Set.
